fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The man found the treasure, hid it again, and in his joy went and sold all he had and bought that field (Matthew 13:44). The field is what he bought, and the treasure was in it.

I get why you'd think so, baker. Selling all you have sounds like a rough Tuesday. But the text says that in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field (Matthew 13:44). So the answer is False.

That's right, friend. The text says that in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field (Matthew 13:44). Gloomy just doesn't fit a man who does it in his joy. I bet his neighbors have questions.

Close, but the text says the opposite, friend. The merchant found one very precious pearl, went away, sold all he had and bought it (Matthew 13:46). Selling all he had is right there in the verse, so the answer is True.

That's it, baker. The net was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish (Matthew 13:47). A net doesn't check IDs at the door. When it was full, the men pulled it ashore and sorted what was in it (Matthew 13:48).
Nope, friend, this net isn't picky. The text says it caught all kinds of fish (Matthew 13:47). That's more than one kind. Think of a big mixed batch, not a single flavor.
Right, baker. The text says they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away (Matthew 13:48). Good and bad are the words the text uses.

I can see the logic, friend. Biggest is often best at a bake sale. But the text says the men sorted the good fish into containers and threw the bad away (Matthew 13:48). Size never comes up in the verse.
Interesting guess, baker. The text says the men sorted the good fish into containers and threw the bad away (Matthew 13:48). Size never comes up in the verse.

That's the one, baker. Jesus says a scribe discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old (Matthew 13:52). Both kinds come out of the same storeroom. New and old are both right there in the verse.
Old things are wonderful, friend. But Jesus says the homeowner brings out new treasures as well as old (Matthew 13:52). The word "new" is right there in the verse. The storeroom brings out both.
Fresh is nice, baker, like a warm batch off the rack. But Jesus says the homeowner brings out new treasures as well as old (Matthew 13:52). The old ones are in that verse too.
